To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) we propose a novel approach to photorealism enhancement that leverages intermediate renderings, 2) we analyze scene layout distributions and find that they are different across datasets, 3) we propose a new training strategy for image to image translation that is based on sampling from a distribution that is similar to the distribution of scene layouts in the training set, 4) we introduce multiple architectural improvements that improve the quality of the photorealism enhancement results
(a) we propose a method that enhances realism of synthetic images; and (b) we introduce a novel adversarial loss, and a strategy for sampling image pairs, which are key components in our approach.
(1) the proposed adversarial objective provides strong supervision at perceptual levels and (2) the proposed patch sampling strategy helps to reduce artifacts in the results.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: (i) What makes a synthetic image look synthetic? (ii) What are the causes of strong visual artifacts? (iii) How can we leverage the strengths of existing rendering pipelines to improve the realism of synthetic imagery? (iv) How can we improve the realism of existing image to image translation techniques?
the problem of enhancing the realism of images produced by computer graphics.
enhancing the realism of rendered images.

the quality of photorealism enhancement can be substantially improved with the use of perceptual supervision, a more realistic training distribution, and a better architecture.
